jamie: Heads-up — after the perf config switch to per-channel calibration + FP8/INT4 kernels on prod-dedicated we see tail latency spikes (~3x p99) on long-context chat workloads. KV cache miss rate jumped ~12%.

leah: Can you paste the perf trace / quick profile dump?

jamie: Sure — short excerpt from the trace (90s window):
```
kernel_select: fp8_mixed_matmul  450us (hot)
kernel_select: int4_mmx         780us (some layers)
kv_cache.lookup          miss_rate=0.18 -> 0.30
batching: avg_batch=22 -> 30 after change
token_latency.p50=12ms p95=48ms p99=210ms (was p99=70ms)
```

miguel: Huh — looks like the int4 kernel latency bimodal for certain layers. Could be calibration causing outlier scales -> overflow/clipping in a few channels, which forces the kernel to take slower code paths (dequant + fallback). Any traces for per-layer quant error?

jamie: We instrumented per-layer scale variance. A small subset (~0.6% layers) have very high per-channel scale spread: stddev/mean > 0.9. Those layers correspond to transformer blocks 10..13.

tess: Also see batching change — avg batch increased and KV warmup seems worse. Bigger batches + those slow layers amplify tail. Maybe our batching heuristic considers gpu_util only, not recent kv_hit trends.

sanjay: Two angles: 1) calibration dataset contains a few outlier sequences that dominate activation ranges; 2) runtime kernel selection needs more nuance (per-tensor fallback when per-channel causes high quantization variance).

leah: For (1) — did we run both per-channel and per-tensor calibration comparisons? We have accuracy deltas but not a focused outlier check.

jamie: Quick diff we ran:
```
per-tensor perf: p99=75ms kv_miss=0.18
per-channel perf: p99=210ms kv_miss=0.30
quality delta (per-channel vs per-tensor): token-EM change ~+0.3% on eval set (so small improvement)
```
So per-channel slightly better quality but huge perf regressions on tail.

miguel: Suggestion: add an outlier filter in calib pipeline. Two-pass: run per-channel calibration, compute per-channel activation histogram stats, drop sequences that push >99.9th percentile of scale shifts, then recompute scales. That should reduce extreme scales but keep most benefits.

tess: Also we can tweak batch caps and kv-warmup policy: reduce max_batch during canary for this model to 16, and increase KV prefetch TTL so hot keys stick around during canary burst.

sanjay: Runtime change we can ship quickly: dynamic per-layer kernel fallback. Heuristic: if per-channel scale variance > 0.5 OR observed kernel latency > threshold, use per-tensor codepath for that layer. We already have kernel fallback infra, just need the variance hook.

jamie: I worry about QA — per-tensor fallback may degrade some small workloads. But given the small eval quality gain you mentioned, probably acceptable as a mitigant while we fix calibration.

leah: Proposed short plan:
- jamie: run two-pass outlier-trim calibration on the existing calib corpus and produce new quant table (today)
- miguel: add variance metric export to the profiling dashboard (tomorrow)
- tess: update canary config to cap batch=16 + KV prefetch TTL (now)
- sanjay: implement per-layer fallback hook behind a feature flag (48h)

ops-bot: Created canary rollout: cedar-001 -> 5% -> metrics: tail_latency, kv_miss_rate, cpu/gpu_util. Canary window 30m.

perf-bot: Uploaded full perf trace https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1718765432 (internal) :mag_right:

jamie: I'll run the two-pass outlier-trim now and post results. If anyone spots a quick test to reproduce locally (short context but with the offending sequences), ping me.

leah: Thanks — good plan. If two-pass reduces scale spikes we can re-evaluate per-channel rollout. Keep the fallback flag ready. :thumbsup:
